title: Unbounded strong-product ratios for the Grundy domination number: paper and checking programs
description:
Final revision of the paper, single column, 9 pages, with its LaTeX source and the programs that recompute its small cases. The paper disproves the conjecture of Bresar, Bujtas, Gologranc, Klavzar, Kosmrlj, Patkos, Tuza and Vizer (2016) that the Grundy domination number of a strong product equals the product of the Grundy domination numbers of its factors, and shows that the ratio is unbounded: graphs on the five-element subsets of an m-element set, bounded through incidence matrices over the fields with two and three elements, give a ratio of at least (m-2)(m-3)(m-4)/(60m). It also computes the Grundy domination number of the graph H_N on {0, ..., N-1} with u and v adjacent when |u-v| = 2 (mod 3), namely floor((N+1)/3)+3 for N >= 6, so that the strong product of H_N with the octahedron is a counterexample for N = 19 (114 vertices) and for every N >= 21. Every statement is proved by hand; no statement rests on the programs.

The counterexample was first made public on 14 October 2026 as release v1.0.0 of creelie/grundy-strong-product (10.5281/zenodo.23378021). An earlier and incomplete version of the paper appeared on Hexagon as hexagon:2610.00494; the revisions v1.2.0 and v1.3.0 of this repository are archived as 10.5281/zenodo.23607502 and 10.5281/zenodo.23629621.
